correctness.rationale: The arbitrary-rank theorem follows from an explicit nondegenerate-form extension lemma: t linear pairing conditions have 2^(2d-t) solutions. For dimensions at least q-1 this supplies outside-span moves through q-1 rounds and more than q candidates on the last move. For d<e, d+1 independent mutually isotropic vectors in the larger space force a linear dependence in the smaller, and a final vector with incompatible prescribed pairings wins in d+2 moves; rank 2 separately detects d=1. The order and exact class count follow. The packaged Python reproduces complete root rank-2,3,4 types for d=1,2,3 and the d=2 claw obstruction.

value.rationale: The exact d+2 first distinguishing depth establishes what a pure graph formula can recover about the Witt index of an infinite classical family. The result simultaneously classifies the entire family at every quantifier rank, gives exactly q-1 classes at depth q>=3, exhibits the sharp exponential finite representative 2^(2(q-1))-1, and explains the 15-to-63-vertex claw transition as the first rank-four witness. This is a uniform structural logical classification, not a finite recomputation or an arbitrary parameter slice.
